pre_event_materials: Repository created before release. Its first commit at 17:55:45 Bangladesh time on 30 August 2026 contained only EVENT.md metadata (team, problem, start code, and repository mapping). No application source was present before 18:00. Original history is preserved; see EVENT.md.

CurrentJabe was reviewed for Bangladesh outage-window terminology, overnight time handling, bilingual electricity copy, and accessible forms. KajChole uses a newly written scheduler, product model, brand, layout, and interface.

The GridGenius university project was reviewed for Bangladesh energy-planning context and time-based data presentation. Its models, prediction API, RAG assistant, datasets, brand, and frontend code are not included.
The pnpm lockfile and minimal Next.js, React, and TypeScript versions match the already-installed sibling submission and required zero new package downloads.

sample_data.method: Built-in demo plus manual entry of published or judge-supplied cases. Copy cuts.start/end and jobs.name/minutes/power into the corresponding controls as described in README.md. No JSON upload; shop_open/shop_close metadata are not applied to the 24-hour planning day.
sample_data.reset_instructions: Select Load demo in the header to restore two outage windows and four jobs (50 generator minutes). To enter another fixture case, remove existing cuts/jobs and enter its values using the forms.

problem_solving_method: Normalize outage windows onto a 1,440-minute day, split overnight windows, and merge overlaps. Place longer grid jobs first outside cuts, then generator and no-power jobs in cut windows where possible or other free time. Prevent overlaps and report jobs that cannot fit. Sum only scheduled generator-job durations after every input change.

R1.evidence: The Set up today panel accepts multiple start and end times in components/planner-app.tsx. normalizeOutageWindows in lib/scheduler.ts maps them onto the aligned 24-hour timeline.

R2.evidence: The Add a job form and editable Job inputs in components/planner-app.tsx capture name, duration, and grid, generator, or no-power need.

R3.evidence: buildDayPlan in lib/scheduler.ts produces non-overlapping placements and blocks grid jobs from outage intervals. Today's plan and Scheduled jobs render the result in components/planner-app.tsx.

R4.evidence: buildDayPlan calculates generatorMinutes from scheduled generator jobs only. The Generator minutes metric updates after every add, edit, or removal. tests/scheduler.test.ts includes an unplaced-generator regression case.

major_design_decisions: Use a deterministic client-side scheduler because P01 supplies every input and does not require prediction.
Protect longer grid jobs first because they have the fewest legal placements.
Prefer outage windows for generator and no-power jobs so the plan uses grid downtime productively.
Keep all four required interactions on one screen so judges can verify them without navigation.
Store the working plan in browser storage so the live demo has no account, database, or API dependency.
known_limitations: The planner creates one non-overlapping job stream and does not model parallel workers or machines.
Jobs must finish within the 00:00 to 24:00 planning day; jobs that cannot fit are shown as unplaced.
Generator minutes represent scheduled generator-job duration, not fuel volume or cost.
Published and judge-supplied cases require manual entry; there is no JSON upload and shop hours metadata do not limit placement.
Longest-first placement is deterministic but does not guarantee optimal packing.
